title: Best Waykar Dehumidifier (2026): 80-Pint, 34-Pint and 150-Pint
h1: The Best Waykar Dehumidifiers, From the 80-Pint to the 150-Pint
dek: Waykar's "80-pint" machine is really a 25-pint machine. Once you know the real numbers, picking the right model gets easy.
description: Is the Waykar 80-pint dehumidifier worth it? Our Waykar picks ranked by real DOE pint ratings and ENERGY STAR efficiency, including the PD160B and pump models.
intro: Waykar is one of the busiest dehumidifier brands online, and the **Waykar 80-pint dehumidifier** is its best-known model — alongside "34-pint," "120-pint" and "150-pint" siblings. Those big numbers aren't invented, but they're measured in a hot, near-saturated test room — 95°F and 90% humidity — that no federal standard uses. Under the Department of Energy's current test, the same machines remove roughly a third as much.

That doesn't make Waykar a bad buy. Many of its models are ENERGY STAR certified, several meet the stricter **Most Efficient** criteria, and the real ratings are public. The trick is to shop by DOE pints and yearly kWh instead of the model name, and to watch for near-identical twins sold at very different prices. We matched every pick below to its ENERGY STAR record so you can see exactly what you're getting.
topPicksLead: For most basements and damp rooms, the **Waykar CHWA80A** is the best pick: about 25 real DOE pints a day, ENERGY STAR Most Efficient, and the lowest yearly energy use of Waykar's "80-pint" family.

products.name: Waykar CHWA80A 80-Pint Dehumidifier
pros: Lowest yearly energy use of Waykar's 80-pint models
Large 1.45-gallon tank plus a gravity drain hose
Auto defrost, auto restart and a 24-hour timer
cons: No pump — needs a floor drain for hands-off use
Coverage claims on the listing are inflated
products.whyWeLoveIt: Strip away the marketing and this is a solid 25-pint dehumidifier with excellent efficiency. It does the same job as Waykar's pricier JD025CE-80 — the two are rated within a hair of each other — while using less power and carrying the Most Efficient badge that its sibling lacks.
products.performance: ENERGY STAR rates it at 24.91 pints a day under the DOE test, with an efficiency of 1.90 liters per kWh and about 260 kWh of electricity a year. That's the right size for a damp room or a small-to-average basement — not the 5,000 square feet the listing claims, which comes from the same inflated test condition. Waykar includes a 3.3-foot drain hose for continuous drainage, plus a filter reminder and auto restart after a power cut. A CHWA80B version adds an automatic swinging louver with identical ratings.
products.notes: Comparing across brands? Our [best 30-pint dehumidifiers](/best/best-30-pint-dehumidifier/) cover the same real-world size class.

products.name: Waykar PD160B-PRO 34-Pint Dehumidifier
pros: Two fan speeds and a 30–80% humidity range
Black and white versions with the same rating
cons: About 10 real pints a day — not for basements
Listing makes wildly overstated savings claims
products.whyWeLoveIt: For a bedroom, bathroom or walk-in closet, a 10-pint machine is plenty, and this one sips power. It also replaces the older PD09B, which never had an ENERGY STAR listing or a published DOE rating.
products.performance: ENERGY STAR rates it at 10.16 DOE pints a day and roughly 144 kWh a year — a modest annual running cost at average US rates. Waykar lists a minimum noise level of 33 dB on low, two fan speeds and a humidity range of 30% to 80%. Ignore the listing's claim of around a thousand dollars a year in energy savings; that's many times more than the unit costs to run in the first place. The black PD160B-PRO-B carries the same certification.

products.whyWeLoveIt: If your only drain is a laundry sink or a window well above the floor, a pump turns a dehumidifier into a set-and-forget appliance. This is Waykar's most efficient full-size unit, and it costs far less than the JD026CE-150PM, which ENERGY STAR rates at virtually the same capacity.
products.performance: ENERGY STAR rates it at 49.43 DOE pints a day with an efficiency of 2.20 liters per kWh and about 471 kWh a year — the best efficiency figure in Waykar's certified lineup. Waykar lists three ways to drain it: the tank, a continuous gravity hose or the built-in pump. The listing doesn't state how high the pump can push water; the related JD026CE-150PM lists 1 to 5 meters. Compare other self-draining units in our [best dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.

blocks.text: Every certified Waykar model has a public ENERGY STAR record listing its DOE capacity, efficiency and yearly energy use. Those records — not the name on the box — are what you should compare.

We don't test dehumidifiers in a lab. For this guide, we matched each Waykar listing to its entry in ENERGY STAR's certified-dehumidifier dataset, which reports capacity under the DOE's 2019 test (65°F and 60% relative humidity), efficiency in liters per kWh, estimated yearly kWh and Most Efficient status.

We then compared drainage options, warranty terms and controls from Waykar's own listings, read owner reviews for recurring problems, and favored the cheaper model whenever two Waykars had essentially identical ratings.

sections.heading: What to look for in a Waykar dehumidifier

items.label: DOE pints, not the model name
items.text: A Waykar "80" is about 25 DOE pints; a "150" is about 49.5. Size the room using our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/).

items.label: The cheaper twin
items.text: The JD025CE-80 and CHWA80A rate within 0.02 pints of each other; the JD026CE-150PM and CTH150PD within 0.04. In both pairs, the less expensive model is also more efficient.

items.label: A pump only if you need lift
items.text: With a floor drain, a gravity hose works fine. Pay extra for a pump only when the drain sits above the unit.

items.label: Most Efficient status
items.text: Three of our four picks meet ENERGY STAR's Most Efficient criteria. Check the dataset yourself if a listing's claim seems off.

items.label: Warranty terms
items.text: Home units list a one-year warranty plus an extra year of extended coverage; the commercial and AFW crawl space units add a five-year compressor warranty.

sections.heading: Waykar 80, 120 and 150 pint dehumidifiers: what the numbers mean

blocks.text: Waykar's listings say outright that their headline capacity is measured at 95°F and 90% relative humidity. Warm, saturated air gives up water easily, so the figure balloons. The pre-2019 federal test used 80°F and 60%; the current one, required since 2019, uses a cooler 65°F and 60% — closer to a real basement.

Waykar's names overstate by 200% or more, so a "150-pint" Waykar competes with other brands' 50-pint machines, not anything bigger.

sections.heading: The Waykar lineup at a glance

blocks.title: Who actually certifies them
blocks.text: ENERGY STAR records list Waykar itself for the CHWA, CTH and PD160B families, but a different company (JHS Inc.) for the JD025CE and JD026CE models, and Zhuhai Invitop Technology for the TDW80 pair. Invitop also certifies AEOCKY units — see our [AEOCKY guide](/best/best-aeocky-dehumidifier/).

sections.heading: Waykar dehumidifier manual, reset and setup tips

blocks.text: Most Waykar questions after purchase come down to finding the manual, getting the unit running again after a stop, and setting it up so it actually drains. A few basics apply across the home lineup.

items: **Find your exact model number** on the rating label on the back or side of the unit. Waykar sells many look-alike models, and the 80-pint manual for a CHWA80A may not match a JD025CE-80 or CTH80D.
**Get the manual** from the product listing where you bought it or from Waykar's customer support, quoting that model number.

**If it stops or won't start,** check that the tank is seated fully and empty (a full or misaligned tank shuts most units off), then unplug it for several minutes and plug it back in. Waykar's home units list auto restart after a power cut, so they should resume your last settings.
**If it runs but collects little water,** the room may already be near your set point, or it may be too cold — see our [not collecting water guide](/guides/dehumidifier-not-collecting-water/).
**For continuous drainage,** attach the hose so it runs downhill all the way to the drain with no kinks or upward loops, then switch drainage mode if your model requires it.

blocks.text: Clean the washable filter every couple of weeks in heavy use; a clogged filter is the most common reason output drops. Our [maintenance guide](/guides/dehumidifier-maintenance/) covers the rest.

The **Waykar CHWA80A** is the best Waykar for most basements: about 25 real DOE pints, top-tier efficiency and a lower price than Waykar's own near-identical JD025CE-80. Choose the **PD160B-PRO** for a bedroom, the **CTH150PD** when you need a pump, and the **CPG130A** only if you want a commercial-style unit and can live with an unverified efficiency claim. For the wider field, start with our [best dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier/) roundup.

faqs.q: Is the Waykar 80-pint dehumidifier worth it?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as you buy it as what it really is: a roughly 25-DOE-pint machine. The CHWA80A version is ENERGY STAR Most Efficient and uses about 260 kWh a year, making it a good fit for a damp room or small basement. Skip the pricier JD025CE-80, which is rated almost identically but uses more power.

faqs.q: What is the best Waykar dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For a basement, the CHWA80A: ENERGY STAR rates it at 24.91 DOE pints a day and 1.90 L/kWh, and it meets the Most Efficient criteria. For a bedroom, the PD160B-PRO; for pump drainage, the CTH150PD.

faqs.q: Why does Waykar call its units 80-pint or 150-pint?
faqs.a: Waykar measures capacity at 95°F and 90% humidity, a condition no federal test uses. Under the DOE's current 65°F/60% test, its "80-pint" models remove about 25 pints a day and its "150-pint" models about 49.5.

faqs.q: Is the Waykar PD160B a good dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For a bedroom, bathroom or closet, yes. ENERGY STAR rates the PD160B-PRO at 10.16 DOE pints a day and about 144 kWh a year, and it meets Most Efficient criteria. It's too small for a basement.

faqs.q: Does any Waykar dehumidifier have a built-in pump?
faqs.a: Yes. The CTH150PD, CHWA150PA and JD026CE-150PM are all 50-pint-class units with pumps, and the CPG130A commercial unit ships with a 16.4-foot pump hose. Waykar's 80- and 34-pint home models drain by tank or gravity hose only.

faqs.q: What do Waykar dehumidifier reviews say?
faqs.a: When you read Waykar reviews, check which model the reviewer actually owns — Waykar sells many look-alike units under similar names — and judge any capacity complaints against the DOE rating rather than the name. A buyer expecting 80 pints a day from a 25-DOE-pint machine in a cool basement will be disappointed; one who sized by the DOE figure usually won't be.

faqs.q: How do I reset a Waykar dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Empty and reseat the water tank, then unplug the unit for several minutes and plug it back in. If it still shows an error code, check the code against your model's manual or contact Waykar support with the model number from the rear label.
Waykar's home units list a one-year warranty, an extra year of extended coverage and lifetime technical support. The AFW crawl space units and CPG130A add a five-year compressor warranty.
